note: The `case` CONSTANT POSITION parity is computed over EXECUTABLE CHILDREN ONLY. A `comment` is a named child, so one comment inside a `case` shifts every later index by one — and then a real BODY lands on an even index and is skipped as if it were an unevaluated constant, taking every relationship inside it with it. metabase/dev/src/dev/kondo_ratchet.clj:343 is the proof: its `case` has TEN named children because of one `;;` at index 6, so the body at index 8 — `(do (when … (.charAt sb (inc i)) …))` — was dropped and the `uses` edges at 348-349 vanished from the graph. Two edges in one file is a small loss; the rule is wrong for every `case` in every corpus holding a comment, and it was invisible because the differential mirror had the IDENTICAL bug — both sides agreed on a body that neither one walked. Two wrong implementations of one rule is not a check. The fix NARROWED the parity, it did not remove it: `with-comment` and `without-comment` must now emit the same three edges, a list-shaped DEFAULT is still an expression (W23), and a list in a genuine constant position is still a group of unevaluated constants and is still skipped (F7).
